INTRODUCTION

JOURNEY

A LIFETIME OF HUMAN LIFE

I have never had the opportunity to meet the author Nguyen Phong. Before that, I knew him as a world-famous scientist who also adapted and rewrote classic cultural and spiritual works that many generations of Vietnamese readers, including me, have always loved.

More than five years ago, I had the opportunity to talk with author Nguyen Phong about the mysteries related to the famous mysterious work Journey to the East - a work that was born nearly half a century ago but no one in the world could find the original, leaving many generations of readers wondering and causing an American publisher to translate it into English from the original Vietnamese that Nguyen Phong adapted. I have come to a broader understanding of the meaning of adaptation - being able to write according to my subconscious, with knowledge and life's contemplations. And I have realized that there are Vietnamese people who are extremely humble but not inferior to anyone in this big world.

I have been fortunate to have him share many stories over the years. Late one night in 2016, during a conversation that lasted into the morning, I asked him about Karma and Reincarnation. He recounted a predestined relationship that happened many years ago, about Thomas - a famous businessman in New York - and his past life stories.

I was extremely surprised and had a premonition that this story was related to my previous concerns, and probably those of many people. I really hope author Nguyen Phong can rewrite those stories into a book. He remained silent and did not answer, nor did he mention this matter in subsequent conversations. After more than two years, I suddenly received an email from him, which contained the first chapters of the book that he named Lifetime of Life. After reading it, I thought to myself that there couldn't be a more accurate name. I know that in the past two years you have flown to New York many times, interviewed and talked with Mr. Thomas to work on the book. Previously, author Nguyen Phong contacted Mr. Thomas to ask for advice about writing a book retelling the past life stories he shared. At first, he was not sure that Mr. Thomas would accept, because many of the stories were too personal and sensitive, but surprisingly, Thomas agreed.

Lifetime of Life is a large picture with countless pieces of life, a massive, vivid film about mysterious lives, stretching from the mighty Atlantis civilization to the ancient Egyptian kingdom of powerful Pharaohs, to today's United States of America - where the main character Thomas, author Nguyen Phong's longtime confidant - is alive.

Human Life provides readers with a new, endless treasure trove of human knowledge revealed for the first time, along with erudite analyzes and surprising predictions about the present and future of the world by wise sages. The important message throughout the work that awakens people is the origin and way of operating the law of Cause and Effect and Reincarnation of the universe. Life seems very long but it passes very quickly, birth, prosperity, and death, as fragile as water waves. The Law of Cause and Effect is extremely precise, detailed, and complex, collected over many lifetimes, interrelated and closely intertwined with each other. No one can calculate how this merit can eliminate that karma, no one can know when the cause will bear fruit. But, once you have caused the cause, you will definitely reap the results

- the law of Cause and Effect has never been wrong.

The invisible impulses and energies of the universe through the laws of Samsara and Karma have created the conditions for this person to meet the other person.

Meeting each other is sometimes fate, sometimes it is debt; Sometimes we meet to repay debts, sometimes to reconnect with old relationships. There are so many things that happen in life that seem random but are actually pre-arranged.

Samsara is a vast school, where all humans and all creatures must learn their own lessons until they are truly perfect. If you refuse to study or have not learned completely, you will be forced to study again, exactly according to the law of Cause and Effect. Some people have the opportunity to witness the law of Karma or Reincarnation, some do not, it depends on each person's fate, perception, experience and belief.

A sincere gratitude to author Nguyen Phong - who worked hard to write this special book - is not enough. Through our conversations, I realized he had only one wish when writing this book. Thank you Mr. Thomas - for everything. Please share with readers his most profound and passionate thoughts:

“ Currently, the world is going through a period of chaos and turmoil, and in fact, every country is suffering from the karma they have caused in the past. Each country, as well as every individual, has its own karma due to the causes they have caused. Individuals has its own individual 'karma', but the nation has 'collective karma' that everyone living in it must pay

Look around the world today with more than seven billion people, how many people are acting cruelly and inhumanely? How cruel are some nations treating others? How many tragic deaths and tragic lives of many innocent people have been happened? Think about it, if everyone were willing to learn and understand clearly Cause and Effect, knowing clearly that once you sow, you will reap what you reap', would anyone dare to act like that? Usually, when people act, they rarely think about the consequences, but once the consequences happen, what do they think and do? Do they resent, blame heaven, blame the earth, blame the people around them for causing those consequences? How many people know how to contemplate, blame themselves and change? That is the motivation for me to share these stories that have never been told to anyone - even though there are unpredictable things - and to allow him to share these unprecedented experiences and lessons with his friends, to write a book for many people around the world to contemplate - while the planet is experiencing many disasters and upheavals. every day. I hope we - the fragile, fluttering little butterfly wings can also create powerful hurricanes to awaken everyone.

What the future of each person, each organization, each country and this planet will be like in the coming period depends on the attitude, perception and awakening of each individual, each organization, each country that country creates. If you want to change, you need to start with awareness, shifting consciousness, spreading love and sharing understanding from each of us first.

Don't wait to see cause and effect to believe it. Cause and effect are road signs, helping people find goodness.

- Nguyen Van Phuoc

Founder of First News - Tri Viet

INTRODUCTION

TAIPEI

AFFINITY

In 2008, I had the opportunity to attend a scientific conference in Taipei.

On that occasion, I contacted a close friend, Professor Raymond Yeh, to visit him. Professor Yeh is the former Head of the Department of Computer Science at the University of Texas and the University of Maryland. He is a scientist, the author of many research papers and ten textbooks taught in universities in the United States. He trained many generations of today's famous scientists and professors. Although he has retired and lives in Taipei, he continues to work in the field of science and has great influence in the world. Professor Yeh happily invited me to visit his home for dinner. The surprising thing was that at that meal there was also the presence of astronaut Edgar Mitchell [1] and a friend of his named Thomas K, who also came to visit Professor Yeh.

Professor Yeh started by introducing everyone:

- Astronaut Edgar Mitchell is a brilliant scientist with many famous research projects on space at Harvard University and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). He was one of six people who set foot on the moon with the Apollo 14 spacecraft on January 31, 1971. On the journey back to earth, looking through the window of the spacecraft, he saw how small the earth was compared to the vast universe and suddenly experienced a strange, indescribable feeling of peace.

When he returned, he found every way to learn about that feeling. As a scientist, Edgar Mitchell tried to explain this strange peace through scientific theories but was unsuccessful. He gathered a number of famous scientists and established an institute to research the relationship between science and inner experience (Institute of Noetic Science); But over the years, these most eminent scientists have not been able to come to any conclusion. Therefore, this time I invited him to meet Venerable Thanh Nghiem, hoping that he could help him answer his questions about this experience.

During dinner that night, we talked intimately about the scientific theories that had just been invented at that time. I found astronaut Mitchell to be open-minded, with a broader and deeper understanding than other scientists I met.

Mr. Mitchell said:

- The latest scientific discoveries today are forcing humanity to change their way of thinking and concepts, even what we previously thought was true. There are more and more new discoveries and new data that can completely change the scientific foundation that we have built for hundreds of years. For example, for centuries we have believed that the earth is the center of the universe and that all planets, including the sun and moon, orbit the earth. Of course we now know that this is completely wrong. The sun is just the center of a solar system, our earth and related planets all revolve around the sun. However, the universe is extremely large and there are many other solar systems that we do not know about. According to estimates by the American Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), there are more than one billion solar systems in the vast universe, of which our solar system is only a small part.

Mr. Mitchell suddenly mused, his voice emotional:

- Only when humans go into space can we truly see how small we are in this unimaginably vast universe. Currently, we know that life has been present on this earth for millions of years, but who knows, life may also exist on other planets or other solar systems.

We think that humans are the most intelligent when compared to animals, but maybe there are creatures on other planets that are even more intelligent that we have never known about.

Not long ago, we thought that the smallest object in the world was a (Molecule) molecule, but then we found the (Atom) atom and thought that the atom was the smallest object. Today, we know that atoms are not the smallest, but that there are much smaller quantum particles (Quark) . If we continue to research there will probably be even smaller things. Therefore, our knowledge is always changing according to new scientific discoveries. If we can prove that (Neutrino) particles move faster than the speed of light, then Einstein's concept of Relativity must change and the orbits of all planets in the universe will be completely different from what we measure today.

He paused and emphasized each word:

- The question is how will we react to the newly discovered facts? Do we accept that what we have believed in for so long are just theories that are no longer valid? Or do we still cling to old concepts because we consider them to be the absolute truth?

Professor Yeh agreed and continued:

- Experimental science is just a collection of knowledge gathered from many experiments, with data measured, observed and verified. As scientists, we always search, learn and research based on theory, pose hypotheses, and then prove whether they are right or wrong. Everything we build relies entirely on measurement tools; But with the advancement of science, as these tools become more sophisticated and more accurate, we will find new data to supplement previous data and continue to build today's science. Strictly speaking, experimental science is an ever-changing process to supplement previous imperfections.

Mr. Mitchell smiled:

- But there will be a time when we find data that is completely different from the previous data. We will set up new hypotheses to change current concepts and we will have a scientific revolution that will overthrow everything we have built before.

Suddenly, Mr. Mitchell turned and asked me:

- You are also a scientist, so what do you think?

I thought, then answered:

- Such a scientific revolution probably needs more than introducing a new theory to overthrow previous theories. In my opinion, first of all, we have to reexamine previous concepts to find out why they are no longer true. As Professor Yeh said, if we invent more sophisticated, more precise tools, then we understand that previous tools were not perfect. If we can prove that these new data are more valid, more accurate, more valid, then we can provide evidence to justify this new theory and replace the previous theory that is no longer valid. However, I think it will probably take a long time to change people's minds.

We continued to discuss scientific discoveries, but mostly it was a conversation between astronaut Mitchell and professor Yeh.

Mr. Thomas and I just sat and listened, sometimes adding a few social sentences.

I saw Mr. Thomas paying attention to the conversation, occasionally smiling but not saying anything. Perhaps because he is a businessman and not a scientist like us, he is more reserved.

After the meal, Mr. Mitchell asked me:

- Tomorrow we will go to see Venerable Thanh Nghiem, do you want to go with us?

Of course I cannot refuse such a rare opportunity.

This pre-arranged meeting took place at the Taipei University lecture hall for a number of students and professors to attend. Professor Yeh was the host of the talk.

Professor Yeh started the meeting:

- Mitchell, please tell about your strange experience flying in outer space to Venerable Thanh Nghiem and ask him about your questions.

Astronaut Mitchell spoke:

- Dear Venerable, after completing the mission on the moon, we began to fly back to earth. When flying in space, our spacecraft must continuously rotate along the 360-degree axis to reduce the heat emitted from sunlight.

Therefore, every two minutes I see the earth, moon and sun through the spacecraft's glass window. I must also add that in space, because there is no atmosphere, we see the planets very clearly. While on earth, we look up at the sky and see stars twinkling due to the influence of the atmosphere; But in space, everything is bright and clear like a giant network with thousands and thousands of stars that look like shining diamonds. It was a wonderful image for us astronauts at that time. Today, everyone can see this image through the Hubble telescope, or through images taken by the US Aeronautics and Space Administration and posted online. If we observe carefully, we will see that the universe is extremely beautiful, no words can describe it.

As a scientist, I know that all the cells, atoms in my body, or the bodies of my friends in the spacecraft, and even the atoms that make up the spacecraft, all originate from our planet or the origin in the universe. All physical phenomena originate from this universe. From then on, I realized that my body and all things in the universe are no different. Instead of being an independent individual, a separate component, I am aware that everything has the same origin. At that moment, my whole body suddenly shook violently. I found myself immersed in a strange, indescribable feeling of peace. This experience continues every time I'm not busy. As astronauts, of course we are very busy because we have to both control the spacecraft and complete scientific experiments in the spacecraft, but sometimes I also stop to look out the window to admire the magical beauty of the universe and feel this strange feeling of peace.

With each rotation of the spacecraft, I see the earth, the moon, the sun, and the sparkling stars. I see the universe as a net with millions of stars emitting brilliant light, and I am clearly aware of the concept of "all things are one".

I understand that if we are unified with everything, then all things are closely related to each other and cannot be separated. This is a new concept that none of us scientists have thought of before.

During that special peaceful experience, I asked myself: "Who am I really?

Where did I come from? Where will I go? How was the universe formed and how is it related to the earth and the people who live there? Did we, the first people to travel into space, feel a clear correlation between humans and the universe, different from the ideas of people who have never left the earth?".

From this concept, I think that perhaps it is time to find a way to change the narrow prejudiced concepts that have imprisoned many generations up to now with a new concept of the relationship between humans and the universe. Perhaps the laws of science and the knowledge established since ancient times will have to change when we look back at everything we have done on this earth, after witnessing our smallness compared to the vast universe. Even modern science that began about four hundred years ago with Isaac Newton will have to change when humans step out of the influence of earth's gravity.

When thinking about that, I suddenly thought of pioneers like Copernicus, Galileo and other prominent scientists who gave opinions on the correlation between the earth and the universe but had to endure opposition and discrimination from short-sighted and narrow-minded concepts at that time. Some were burned alive, some were imprisoned until death, but the truth is still the truth, undeniable. All conservative and narrow-minded tendencies must change when people know how to raise their eyes, erase old prejudices and open their hearts to see the vast universe.

Astronaut Mitchell paused to think, then continued:

- When returning to earth, I always wonder about this strange feeling of peace

. I read a lot of scientific books but couldn't find anything that could explain the above phenomenon. I turned to researching Western religious books but couldn't find anything. I sought out wise scholars but no one could answer my questions. A friend advised me to read documents about Eastern religions, and I began to study Buddhism, especially books about samadhi (Samadhi). I see a similarity between the experience I had in space and the experience of the Eastern sages, when they described the state of meditation.

Professor Yeh suddenly asked:

- Is that feeling like feeling one with all things?

Astronaut Mitchell replied:

- That's right, at that time I didn't see any difference between myself and everything else. The feeling of harmony, vibrating with the movement of the universe, is a strange experience that cannot be described in words.

Professor Yeh turned to ask Venerable Thanh Nghiem:

- Dear Venerable, according to Buddhist concepts, is astronaut Mitchell's experience of no longer seeing the distinction between himself and all things an enlightenment?

The Venerable Thanh Nghiem smiled and looked at Mr. Mitchell:

- First of all, I am very happy that astronaut Mitchell had a special experience. Among thousands, tens of thousands of people, not many people have such an experience. In life, when people experience something completely new that can completely change previous personal experiences, we can consider it as an enlightenment. However, it could also be just a temporary feeling.

For example, not long ago, one of my disciples also had a special experience. After a seven-day meditation retreat, he returned home. On the way back, he saw all the trees and flowers, from tiny insects to leaves and blades of grass, happily welcoming him. He felt a wonderful peace as if integrating with the outside world and believed that he had attained enlightenment. He hurried back to tell me about that experience.

I told him that although it was a wonderful moment of experience, it could also disappear in an instant. Don't take that feeling as a realization. If you don't believe it, try going back to that garden to see if the plants, flowers, and animals welcome you like before.

When he returned, he did not feel the same experience as before, so he asked: "How can I get that wonderful feeling back?". I replied: "No one can forever possess that past experience. If you want to hold on to it forever, you are greedy. Having this experience is just a result of the practice process. It is not the enlightenment you expected.

The purpose of practicing meditation is to develop wisdom and eliminate ego. If we reach the state of Selflessness, will this world still exist? If we reach the state of non-discriminating Mind, then where is there still us or this world? For most people, this world really exists, but for those who are enlightened, this world is just an illusion, not real, so all experiences, no matter what they are, are just temporary illusions. We should not pay attention to it or want to hold on to it forever. consciousness, will change, because all things will change. Even though it exists as it is, let's still consider it as just phenomena of the mind.

However, for those who have experienced, then completely changed their perception and always lived with that consciousness, we can conclude that that person has attained enlightenment, according to the Buddhist concept, this person has had a good "cause" from before and now it has begun to blossom “fruit”.

The Venerable Thanh Nghiem continued to share:

- Astronaut Mitchell is a scientist, but that experience cannot be explained by scientific reasoning, cannot be proven through experiments, or create theories using logical methods. He believes that this is new knowledge that science needs to explore and research further. However, you should know that that feeling is a spiritual experience within the category of religion that science cannot explain. Neither philosophy nor logic can explain it, because it is a spiritual experience that happened to only one person - you.

That experience completely changed his way of thinking.

From then on, he felt it became a part of him and could no longer be separated. This experience is beyond the scope of science because those who experience it cannot describe it, explain it, cannot prove it, and no one else has the same experience, it is a personal experience. Whoever drinks water knows for himself whether it is hot or cold. In his case, he alone felt the peace of personal harmony with the universe, merging with all, no longer distinguishing between himself and the universe. There were also other astronauts in the spacecraft at that time. Why can't they have the same experience as you? Why was he the only one who felt that way? If speaking according to science, once he feels something, everyone else must also see it.

In short, this is something that science cannot explain or prove, because it is outside the scope of science.

Professor Yeh continued asking:

- Mr. Mitchell, will that strange experience come back to you again?

When you return to earth, do you still have that feeling?

Astronaut Mitchell replied:

- Yes, I can still feel and live in this boundless peace. It completely changed my concept of humans and the universe, so I sought to explain it in terms of science, logic, philosophy and spirituality. I agree with Venerable Thanh Nghiem about what he taught; But as a scientific researcher, I still want to find a way to connect science with internal experience, to open up a new horizon for humanity's lacking knowledge today.

Professor Yeh continued to ask:

- What do you think about today's flawed scientific theories?

For example, the hypothesis of the formation of the universe through the Big Bang?

Astronaut Mitchell replied:

- Experimental science is built from theories, then proven through experiments with accurate data. Although the hypothesis of the formation of the universe through the Big Bang is accepted by most, no one has been able to prove it accurately. Therefore, it is still just a hypothesis. It explains some phenomena, but it is not complete enough to be recognized as absolute truth. In my opinion, with the advancement of science today, this hypothesis may become outdated when more evidence or data becomes available. I don't think the universe is just the result of an explosion, but something that moves and changes constantly, so it's very difficult to define clearly.

Professor Yeh raised the question:

- But if we eliminate the theory of the Big Bang, does it mean that time does not begin from the creation of the universe but is something that has no beginning?

Astronaut Mitchell explained further:

- For me, time is only a relative measurement.

It was humans who proposed the so-called "time" on this earth, but nature does not divide it like that. Humans create the concept of time, then divide it into many fragments.

Earth rotates once around the sun, which is considered a year, then a year has twelve months, each month has a number of days, then days are divided into hours, hours are divided into minutes, minutes are divided into seconds, etc. This division is only limited on earth. If we go to Mars or Venus, we will have to change time differently. If we continue to go into space, time on earth will no longer be valuable.

Professor Yeh turned to ask Venerable Thanh Nghiem:

- The Venerable Bach, a space scientist and a famous astronaut like Mr. Mitchell, does not completely believe in the hypothesis of the creation of all things through the Big Bang, but believes that the universe is something that is always changing. If so, do all things have no beginning or end, but are just a constantly changing process? Venerable Master, is this concept different from the Buddhist concept in the Hoa Avatamsaka Sutra?

The Venerable Thanh Nghiem replied:

- Up to now, everyone believes that all things were formed from

the Big Bang. Scientists also rely on this hypothesis to make scientific theories about space, time, etc. I'm glad that an eminent scientist and famous astronaut like you thinks differently. He believed that the universe is always changing and constantly moving, so it fits very well with the concept of "formation, existence, destruction, destruction" because all things and phenomena are always changing, without beginning or end. This is very consistent with the concept of Buddhism.

However, I would like to add that the Buddhist cosmology does not divide time and space as two distinct entities but includes both time and space. Time includes past, present and future. Space also covers all six directions (East, West, South, North, above, below). But does time really exist? Are not! Time is only created when an object in space moves, and if we can measure that movement, then time exists. In other words, if we feel space changing, time exists. If space did not move, there would be no time. But saying that, does space exist? Neither! If we cannot perceive time, space does not exist. Everything is just something primordially empty.

In other words, the Buddhist universe is a combination of space and time. If this exists then that exists, if this doesn't then that doesn't, all are interconnected, interdependent and closely integrated. In short, all things in the universe are relative, meaning they are impermanent, selfless and dependent.

Even though time and space have different names, they share the same essence, or "all things are one", one is all, all is one.

The Venerable Thanh Nghiem continued to explain:

- Today, space physics has proven this with Albert Einstein's Theory of Relativity. Especially the concept of four-dimensional space, clearly stating the meaning: space and time are not two absolute things with separate entities, but are only relative.

It is correct to use the word "space-time" to refer to both, because their nature is to be interconnected, harmonize with each other as one, capture and integrate with each other in a wonderful way.

With his superior mind, Einstein discovered the Law of Relativity, seeing that speed, time, space, and mass are all relative, not absolute. His formula E = mc 2 proved that energy is the mass of that object when moving as fast as the speed of light. At that time, matter will turn into energy and when the energy slows down, it will turn into matter.

The Venerable Thanh Nghiem turned to astronaut Mitchell and said clearly:

- As you know, energy is mass and mass is also energy, or spirit is matter and matter is spirit. That is exactly what the Buddha taught in the Avatamsaka Sutra more than twenty-five hundred years ago: "Mind is matter, matter is also mind - all things are one, that is the principle 'the dharma realm of things is unobstructed'". If you want to communicate with this Avatamsaka realm, you must enter through the spiritual door, but feelings of discrimination or logic based on the contemplation of "consciousness" are not possible. Only the spiritual door can synthesize time and space, bringing him into a "constantly moving" life.

Earlier, he said that he did not believe that this universe was formed by the Big Bang, but that this universe is constantly changing. But who can sense such a change in the universe? Is it human? Other creatures are not as intelligent as humans, so they are not as aware of the universe as humans. Humans have a clear idea of ​​time and space.

When time exists, space also exists, that is the basic concept of the creation of the universe.

The Venerable Thanh Nghiem turned to speak to Professor Yeh:

- Just now, you asked if this concept coincides with the concept of the Hoa Adornment Sutra? That's right, the policy of the Flower Nghiem Sutra is "the dharma realm of dependent origination", meaning that everything, everything is created by the harmony of causes and conditions, everything depends on each other, causes give birth to effects, effects give birth to causes, layers overlap, sometimes interconnect, sometimes oppose, and influence each other to be born, nothing can exist on its own or be independent. This exists thanks to that, that exists thanks to this. The layers of overlap do not end, so it is called "coincidence and dependent origination".

Therefore, "one is all, all is one", everything, everything is closely related to each other, obeying the laws of the universe such as impermanence and non-self. The special feature of the Hoa Adornment Sutra is that it talks about the "dynamic" nature of the universe, whose characteristic is constant transformation and change.

The Venerable Thanh Nghiem looked at everyone and emphasized:

- This change is also a characteristic of our impermanent lives that not many people pay attention to. We are born, grow up, then grow old and die. Every second, every minute, our bodies change with tens of thousands of cells dying and tens of thousands of cells being born. Change is measured over time and divided into three periods: "Past, present and future". Actually, this division is only relative because one period can still talk about other periods. The three times can be separate or mixed together, change or be interconnected. For example, when we think, we can be aware of many things in the past, present, or future.

Everything and everything in the universe interacts with each other according to causes and conditions and creates things and things. This impact and transformation progresses and changes continuously in the biochemical cycle. It is thanks to this division of time that we can clearly understand the laws of Impermanence, Selflessness, Dependent Origination and Cause and Effect. The Flower Nghiem Sutra explains to us clearly that the universe was created by infinite dependent origination, although the appearances are different, they all share the same essence, equality and interconnection. This essence is the true mind.

From suchness arise all things. Everything that exists is an illusion, yet we consider it real.

Thanks to knowing how to observe the true form through profound meditation, we can understand and see everything clearly, everything as it is. When we practice looking deeply at things, we go beyond the external appearance to clearly see the inner being. When we know how to direct our minds higher, beyond the world of difference phenomena to reach this realm of no difference, then we can clearly understand the true nature of things.

Professor Yeh asked astronaut Mitchell:

- The Venerable presented the creation of the universe through the lens of Buddhism. As a space scientist, what do you think about this concept?

Astronaut Mitchell replied:

- There are many different concepts about the creation of the universe. Even

The wisest scientists do not agree with each other, some say this, some say that. One person came up with this theory, another person came up with another concept. All are hypotheses, no one has been able to clearly prove them with accurate data. However, if you say everything is "No", most people will misunderstand that it is nothing, and if you say the universe is not real, no one will believe it. The more we learn about these things, the more scientists, like myself, become confused. Let's assume that the universe is something that really exists, but how will science explain it? Who created it? Where does it come from? How did it start? Experimental science requires proof, explanation, coming up with theories, and then finding data to prove whether that theory is true or false.

The twentieth century is the century of many inventions, and people have discovered many things that were only imagined before, but have now come true. Currently there are many new theories and new concepts, more than all the theories up to now. It must be said that humanity has gone very far, set foot on the moon, entered space, but there are so many other things we don't know yet. The explanation of the universe is still something that scientists like us do not fully understand.

However, this concept of communication and inclusion, not division, is a concept that is very consistent with quantum physics theory. For many years now, we have been researching the use of the scientific tools of quantum physics to explore the correlation between science and spirituality. Of course, we have not come to any clear conclusion, but there is a lot of evidence that quantum physics will take experimental science further than before.

Professor Yeh wondered:

- If so, will the Big Bang theory no longer be valid?

Astronaut Michell shared:

- Not only me but other scientists also think so.

There has been much evidence that this hypothesis is not as complete as people think. There have been many scientific studies that have found new data that contradicts the data about the Big Bang. Of course, many more experiments are needed before we can draw clear conclusions.

But in my opinion, as science develops every day, people will find a lot of new data to prove that some previous theories are no longer true. For example, in the past, Einstein believed that the speed of light was absolute, nothing could go faster than the speed of light. The quantum physics concept of "quantum non-locality" proves that there are signals that can travel faster than the speed of light. In the Extrasensory Perception (ESP) experiment, when a thought occurs, others can recognize it immediately. I performed this experiment on the moon and people on earth immediately received these signals, not just once but dozens of times. If we measure time and distance, these signals travel much faster than the speed of light. According to the quantum physics concept of "non-locality", sensory signals, or more simply thoughts originating from the human brain, can move at unlimited speed.

Professor Yeh added:

- One element of the concept of "non-locality" is the theory of non-locality

correlation between two entities. If one entity vibrates or feels something, the other entity also notices immediately. Although this is still just a scientific hypothesis, it can also be used to explain sympathy between two people or the concept of Cause and Effect.

Astronaut Mitchell nodded:

- Yes, the Buddhist concept of Cause and Effect is very suitable for today's scientific theories. Physics has proven that if we throw an object into the air, that object will have to fall because of the earth's gravity. Similarly, an action will also bring about a result. Any driving force has an opposite reaction. Today, all scientists accept this concept.

Professor Yeh continued to ask questions to Venerable Thanh Nghiem:

- Venerable Bach, astronaut Mitchell has just explained the relationship between two entities. So how can this explain karma in the Buddhist theory of Cause and Effect?

The Venerable Thanh Nghiem replied:

- According to Sanskrit, Karma means action. Any action such as gesture ( body), speech (mouth) or thought (mind) also creates a reaction or karma. However, it must be added that these actions must be based on consciousness ( consciousness). Therefore, between karma (karma) and consciousness have a close correlation with each other, similar to the scientific hypothesis about quantum correlation that astronaut Mitchell just presented.

Consciousness belongs to the mental category. Buddhism has many explanations about consciousness. According to the Vijnanamatra sect, consciousness can be divided into many detailed parts, but we can temporarily divide consciousness into six parts: eye, ear, nose, tongue, body and mind, corresponding to the six senses of eye, ear, nose, tongue, body and brain. In addition, there is the seventh consciousness or base consciousness ( Mana consciousness ) and the eighth consciousness is store consciousness ( A la da consciousness ).

Karma is created by the sixth consciousness ( consciousness ) because it creates distinction, so it is also called discrimination consciousness. This sixth form distinguishes between right and wrong, good and bad, right and wrong, etc. The previous five consciousnesses (eye, ear, nose, tongue, body) do not differentiate, just perceive sensations, so they do not create karma.

When these feelings take place, the sixth consciousness gives rise to distinct ideas and cooperates with the seventh consciousness or base consciousness ( Mana consciousness) to create karmic causes. When a karma occurs, it can bring about an effect at this moment or it can happen at another time. A cause can produce an effect in this life or it can wait until the next life. However, whatever you do is what you reap.

If you plant beans, you can eat beans, if you plant melons, you can eat melons. It is impossible to grow beans and produce melons. Karma caused in this life is sometimes stored in the eighth consciousness or store consciousness and acts in the next life.

In other words, from life to life, the only thing that is maintained is the cause, or seed, stored in the store consciousness.

This eighth form contains all the seeds of karma and they continue to follow each individual like a shadow and image, from life to life.

According to the Buddhist concept, human life is formed by three entities: life force, warmth and store consciousness. Life force helps people live, warmth is the movement of life force that creates energy, and store consciousness affects everyone's life according to the law of Cause and Effect. When vitality dries up, people will grow old and die. At death, warmth is lost and the last thing to go is store consciousness. It will lead people to life in another life.

Because in daily life people create good or bad karma through actions, words and thoughts, the seeds of this karma are stored in the store consciousness. Some seeds operate continuously, influencing the above seven consciousnesses, forming an individual's temperament, talents, and habits because any action (karma) also creates reactions (karma).

However, some seeds hidden in the store consciousness do not activate immediately but wait for another convenient time, so people continue to experience one life after another. When there are enough conditions, these seeds activate according to the law of Cause and Effect in a different form. The body can be a human being, or it can also be an animal due to the guidance of karma.

According to Buddhist concepts, the current life is not the first or last life, but we have lived hundreds, millions of previous lives and will have countless more lives to come. Human life is limited, lasting at most eighty or one hundred years, but store consciousness never ends, it lasts continuously and that is the endless cycle of reincarnation that the Buddha clearly pointed out in his teachings.

Of course, saints are different, because they have been freed from the influence of karma. They knew how to practice to end the cycle of birth and death, and that was the ultimate goal that Buddha recognized and taught to humanity. The mission of Buddhism is to be liberated from the influence of the cycle of Samsara.

Professor Yeh continued to ask questions to further clarify the words shared by Venerable Thanh Nghiem:

- Venerable Monk, so how to neutralize these karmic forces?

The Venerable Thanh Nghiem replied:

- If people know how to transform the eighth consciousness (A re da consciousness), turning consciousness into wisdom, they will go beyond the control of karma. This requires diligent cultivation, and that is the only way. Of course, there are many ways to practice. Some people like to practice Zen, some like to practice Pure, some like to practice Secret, etc., depending on each person's ability.

Professor Yeh asked further:

- The Venerable shared very clearly about Karma, Cause and Effect and the cycle of Samsara, but as a scientist, what do you think about this, astronaut Mitchell?

Astronaut Mitchell replied:

- From a scientific perspective, we do not have a clear explanation of Karma as Venerable Thanh Nghiem just presented. We do not yet have any scientific tools to explain Karma or prove that there is an afterlife. We can still read books and learn about this concept, but we cannot measure it or prove it. However, I agree that any action creates a reaction. Therefore, science can recognize the concept of the law of Cause and Effect, but storing these forces somewhere, then letting them arise at another time is something we cannot prove in the laboratory.

In my opinion, the current concept of Reincarnation is still something that cannot be explained by science. We know that since ancient times, every country and every civilization in the world has had beliefs that science cannot explain today. Whether that concept is right or wrong, whether it is valid or not, is something that science cannot verify. Therefore, we can only consider them as beliefs. People can believe one thing or another, but it cannot be proven with laboratory data. However, as someone who has had an experience that can only be explained spiritually but not scientifically, I have another thought.

In my opinion, religious faith and scientific theory can complement each other and create new theories, that is the power of new knowledge. Buddhism believes that everything is created by causes and conditions, from "No" to "Yes". Science also knows that when energy solidifies, it forms matter. In other words, matter is made up of energy. Therefore, we can use our senses to perceive matter, I can see, I can touch matter - like this table or this chair. The understanding of energy and matter is a science based on human intelligence. We can think of intelligence as the ability to recognize based on facts. From there, we can come up with new scientific laws, or new nouns, to explain the correlation between humans and the universe.

Although science has progressed a lot, there are still many things we need to discover. To learn more about these things, we need to use advanced scientific tools, new theories, to discover more and develop human knowledge. Who knows, maybe one day science will be able to explain and prove Buddhist theories, and the two will complement each other to promote human progress.

The Venerable Thanh Nghiem continued:

- It's not that simple. I want to make it clear that science and Buddhism are two completely different environments. Although the two have some similarities, science can never explain the profound and wonderful things of Buddhism. Why? Because the teachings of Buddhism go beyond the ability of language, beyond perceptual awareness, beyond the normal understanding that the senses bring, because it is the deep activities of the mind and not built on intelligence.

Experimental science is completely built on the human senses, which are limited. There are many things that the senses cannot perceive. For example, we cannot hear some sounds with frequencies that are too low or too high.

Our eyes cannot see some things because they vibrate at a different frequency. Even our thinking is very limited because the knowledge we have is completely based on previously accumulated memories, or on things that have been taught. Our thinking is biased. From this limitation comes erroneous theories and narrow prejudices.

Of course, over time, some erroneous theories will be revised and replaced by others. Science can help people develop knowledge and conquer nature, but how can finite things explain infinite things?

Science explains everything based on words, but Buddhist concepts go beyond the limits of words. Science is based on inference, but Buddhist concepts go beyond common reasoning, so they cannot be thought or discussed. If it cannot be described by reason or words, how can science study these limitless things?

Experimental science is based on intelligence through the brain's ability to reason and analyze, but the Buddhist concept is not based on the intelligence of the brain, but is based on another type of intelligence called Prajna wisdom (prajna), so it cannot be explained by intelligence. okay.

However, the progress of science can help us understand more about the immutable laws of the universe, opening everyone's eyes. Science also helps the future development of Buddhism to bring happiness to humanity.

Professor Yeh asked further:

- Astronaut Mitchell, do you agree with that?

Astronaut Mitchell nodded:

- I completely agree with Venerable Thanh Nghiem. Today, we have covered many important issues. Although there are still some differences of opinion, that is not important.

When I see the beauty of the universe, I feel the connection between myself and all things, but I cannot come up with a mathematical equation to explain that event. I felt something strange happen to me, but I didn't know how to explain it.

As a scientist, I am very interested in these unexplained phenomena so I still want to find a more reasonable solution.

I know this is not easy. It may take decades, hundreds of years to explain, or it may never be explained.

However, I want to raise questions and raise issues about the correlation between science and spiritual experience for future scientists to continue researching.

I know that death, rebirth, and karma are extremely important concepts that need to be studied carefully, because I believe they are frontiers that science has not yet reached, but sooner or later we must learn more. I believe that over time, humanity will progress and perhaps one day will achieve a deep understanding of concepts that they currently consider only religious beliefs. If we don't learn and research, I don't know what the future of humanity will be.

Astronaut Mitchell exclaimed:

- When I returned from space to earth with a strange experience, I found myself completely different. I can clearly perceive the current state of humanity. I clearly see brutality increasing everywhere. I felt the suffering of war victims as if it were happening to me. I clearly see the consequences that humans are causing to this earth, such as mercilessly destroying the environment. People are becoming more and more selfish, greedy, insensitive, and indifferent, without seeing the consequences they are causing to themselves, their families, or their country. Therefore, I feel we need to change outdated concepts, move beyond ordinary disputes to move towards something noble and better. Unfortunately, today, my own country is also supporting this evil influence. How can we say that humanity is more civilized than before, more advanced than before while we are not aware of what we are doing?

Professor Yeh continued to ask the question:

- Venerable Sir, we only have a very short life. As astronaut Mitchell just said, can we hope that there will be change in the near future? What will the future of humanity be like?

The Venerable Thanh Nghiem replied:

- I am always optimistic about the future of humanity. Currently, there are more than seven billion people living on this earth. I believe that if there are still thinking people like astronaut Mitchell and they are aware of cruelty, hatred, selfishness, greed... and then find ways to nurture compassion, towards truth, goodness and beauty, they can create positive influences on the people around them.

As long as we have hope for a good future, that future will happen. If we despair, and let things happen, it would be a pity.

Why don't I feel pessimistic? Because not long ago I read a science book about Chaos Theory, in which the author, also a scientist, used an example of the effect of a small fluttering butterfly wing in the Brazilian forest that can cause a major hurricane in Texas. A small thing can create unexpectedly large impacts.

This may explain the current situation. If a person is conscious and does good things, even if they are small, they can create a positive influence, helping to change the people around them. If many people work together to do good deeds, the whole world will change.

The Venerable Thanh Nghiem turned to the students sitting in the audience and emphasized:

- Nowadays, most people are busy with their livelihoods so they are unaware of the consequences of their actions, words and thoughts.

They continue to create karma for themselves and those around them. However, there are still people who are aware of the crisis that is happening and constantly call on people to stay awake, avoid doing selfish, greedy, and hateful things, and often do good things. Even just one or two people who initiate good deeds can influence others, like astronaut Mitchell. I hope the professors and students attending today's talk will be more aware of their work and raise their eyes to a higher level, like astronaut Mitchell is trying to propose to end the usual disputes and current selfish and greedy tendencies, so that we will have a better future.

Astronaut Mitchell spoke:

- I completely agree with the words shared by Venerable Thanh Nghiem. Sometimes I am also pessimistic, but I don't want to be like that.

Professor Yeh concluded the meeting:

- Today we had an interesting and useful talk, but we cannot continue because Venerable Thanh Nghiem still has to return to the temple to prepare for the ceremony. On behalf of the organizing committee, I would like to thank Venerable Thanh Nghiem and astronaut Edgar Mitchell, hoping that in the future we will have more talks like this.

Mr. Thomas continued to ask:

I explain:

- Soul is just a common noun used to name something that exists after this body dies. - If so, according to you, what is the difference between the soul and store consciousness

?

While store consciousness is something living, always changing, it is a collection of many seeds, accumulated through experiences over many lifetimes.

Mr. Thomas nodded as if he was interested in something interesting:

be reborn as another person in the next life. No matter what that person does, he or she will still be reborn as a human being, because the soul is something immortal and unchanging. What do you think about this?

I explained, even though I believed that Mr. Thomas might already know:

- That's right, depending on good or bad conditions, after death, a person can be reborn as a human or an animal. Furthermore, they can also become ghosts, demons or go to hell. Therefore, the cycle of Samsara is not only limited to the human world but also has other realms.

Mr. Thomas smiled and sympathized with me:

- Great! What he said was very interesting and surprised me because there was someone who understood and sympathized. Perhaps we need to meet each other more times to discuss and share about this interesting topic. - It's a surprise to meet you in New York, why did you come without telling me? Luckily, I was lucky to meet you here. We had an appointment and hadn't had a chance to finish the story in Taipei five years ago. Do you want us to continue discussing this topic in depth?

- You give me the hotel address and time you can go, tomorrow I will send someone to pick you up.

- You said you believe in Reincarnation and Karma, but is that just a religious belief or is it something else? As a scientist who is very interested in philosophy and many religions, especially Buddhism, in addition to belief, you must have some evidence, right?

- As a scientist who has researched a lot about Buddhism, I not only simply believe in the Buddha's teachings but have directly experienced, observed, and verified it over a long period of time. I have pondered and scientifically analyzed His teachings for many years and found it very reasonable and explained why it became a truth. Therefore, this is not just a pure belief, although today Buddhism has many variations that are no longer original - even in Asian countries - but many people have realized that many bad people have used Buddhism, Buddhist temples, and Buddhist beliefs to profit and serve their own purposes and interests. Returning to the evidence of Reincarnation, there has been a lot of evidence of reincarnation in lifetimes such as the case of Edgar Cayce, a farmer in Kentucky with no more than a high school education. Only through a serious illness did he remember his previous life, the life in which he was a physician. Not only that, from there he could diagnose and treat diseases more accurately than contemporary doctors. He left behind many valuable medical documents that many medical universities are still researching and applying today.

Mr. Thomas smiled and nodded in agreement:

- I have read some documents about the Edgar Cayce case. This is truly a special case of Reincarnation, but surely there are other cases?

- If we do not completely believe in the cycle of Samsara, how can we explain the case of children with special gifts that we often call prodigies? Who taught such wonderful knowledge to a child not yet ten years old, who had not yet attended elementary school, if he was not born into lives in civilizations that have now disappeared from the face of the earth?

What do you think about a five-year-old boy like Blaise Pascal being able to solve extremely complex math problems, including math equations that gave math masters headaches at that time? How does science explain this case if we do not believe that people have gone through many lives and have been taught and learned in the past?

Mr. Thomas asked:

- Do you think these people can recall the knowledge they have experienced and learned in previous lives? Why can't others remember anything?

I answer:

- If a person is thoroughly trained in a certain expertise and continues to pursue that expertise in many subsequent lives, due to special conditions, they will be able to recall this subconscious knowledge.

For example, writer John Stuart Mill could speak and write fluently in Greek and Latin at the age of four even though he was born in England and his parents only spoke English. Not only that, when he was just eight years old, he wrote a book of nearly eight hundred pages about the history of the dynasties of the Roman kings with dates and years so clear in every detail that historians were surprised at its accuracy.

Going further into the field of literature, we will see that from the age of three, writer Voltaire memorized excellent essays by literary masters who lived in the last century. According to the Buddhist concept, everything we do or think is stored in our store consciousness ( A lai da consciousness) in the form of seeds. When these seeds are activated, it is due to special causes and conditions that are beyond our understanding.

Perhaps you also see that in the same family, with the same parents, raised in the same circumstances, and educated in the same way, why are siblings, each with their own personality, no one the same? Some people like music, some people like science, some people like sports. Some people just listen to the lecture and understand immediately, while others study forever and don't understand anything.

Why is there such a difference? If one does not apply the concept of cause and effect, how should one explain?

Are human temperament and personality influenced by causes, or seeds, planted in the past? A craftsman is good because he has practiced that profession in the past. A student is smart because he has learned that subject before. This may explain why some people are good at math while others are talented at music.

We continued to discuss this topic until late at night and felt very excited because there were many similar ideas. At that time, I was really surprised to learn that this businessman had a very broad knowledge and a special interest in the Law of Reincarnation. He also seemed very open, different from the first meeting.

Mr. Thomas urgently invited me to visit him again every time I had a chance to visit New York. This time I shook his hand and promised to visit him to continue discussing this topic. From that moment on, we became close friends.

Years later I learned why Mr. Thomas was interested in this topic, because he had profound experiences about Samsara through a special case that he recounted to me.

One day in the late fall of 2016, I visited Mr. Thomas at his vacation home in Colorado. That day there were only two people, the conversation started with modern scientific and technological inventions, he asked me:

that within progress lies the seeds of disaster that no one expected? For example, the invention of gunpowder sparked fierce wars. The advancement of atomic science led to the disaster of nuclear war.

Young people today seem to be attracted by a kind of "magic" that drains their vitality and intelligence. In the future, technology will devastate humanity because they will lose many things that previous generations have built. Technology is a double-edged sword, but most people do not understand this clearly. They consider it civilization and progress without knowing that future generations will have to pay a very high price for these inventions that they consider miraculous.

What Mr. Thomas said made me think of the fact that my students today are no longer studying as hard as before.

Mr. Thomas continued:

- Even worse are things like video games. These things have taught young people strange, unusual, unimaginable behaviors. From children to older adults, everyone is fascinated with these dangerous things that most just consider harmless games. No one understands that although technology can bring many benefits, it also has many potential dangers. Young people who do not know how to distinguish and have not been taught carefully should easily become victims of this "magic power". They glue their ears and eyes to the small phone and forget everything happening around them, because they only know how to live in a "virtual world". There are children who forget to eat, forget to sleep and live in this "virtual world", so they cannot grow up, have no responsibility for the world around them, become indifferent and emotionless, because their minds have been "hypnotized".

Although I partly agree with Mr. Thomas's comment, I also add a few words in defense:

- Science and technology have helped people a lot. We need to have an open look at inventions in many fields, instead of blaming the iPhone.

Mr. Thomas laughed:

- Current science and technology still have many shortcomings that need to be supplemented. One cannot teach science and technology without mentioning the ethics or duties of those responsible for working in it. Science without conscience, technology without responsibility will only bring disaster to humanity in the future.

Mr. Thomas exclaimed:

- With too fast a growth rate, with a huge consumer market, with too high an income, it is difficult to slow down the development momentum of these products, thereby leading to mistakes that are difficult to correct. I don't condemn science or technology, I just want to say that what we need to do is develop the ability to distinguish between right and wrong, good and bad, and use intelligence to clearly know the consequences we can avoid.

Mr. Thomas was silent for a moment as if reminiscing about something, then continued:

- Do you know that this has happened many times in the past? Because of lack of awareness, people let these "magical" products drain their vitality. Most people become passive, forgetting everything around them. They no longer live with awareness but have become completely insensitive machines to social situations. A mind that does not know how to think will easily be controlled to do inhumane things. In the future, if people do not know how to use their brains to distinguish between right and wrong, they will become machines that only know how to do what they are told.

Mr. Thomas paused as if to let me think about what he said, then continued with emotional words:

I was silent for a long time. I really didn't expect that a normally quiet person like Mr. Thomas would be so eloquent with such profound comments. What he said is also something I have been wondering about for a long time.
