The next morning, I felt very uncomfortable and frustrated, so I ordered my entourage to saddle the horse for me to go outside the palace. I didn't want the soldiers to follow me, so I ordered them to turn back, then headed straight into the desert alone. The sun began to rise, the sunlight spread over the rolling sand dunes stretching in the desert, making me feel like there was a magical vitality covering everything.

I asked myself: "Where is the sun god Amun Ra now?".

For a long time, I have silently called His name during rituals held in the temple when offering offerings but have never felt His presence. Currently I am standing alone in the middle of a vast desert, without priests or rituals, but only quiet, bare sand dunes, but I find myself thinking of Him more earnestly than ever. I longed to see Him, to talk to Him intimately, hoping He would answer my questions. But it's in vain, up until now he has only been a lifeless statue in the temple of the Sun.

I stopped my horse, quietly looked at the streaks of light running at the end of the horizon and suddenly felt something gentle and soft like the hand of the Sun stretching out to welcome me. As if motivated by something, I knelt down and offered Him a fervent prayer, the prayer of a faithful believer, not of a majestic Pharaoh. Suddenly I found myself immersed in a vast, endless light. I feel something strange is transforming in my mind.

It seems like the Sun is teasing me, toying with me? I've wanted to find Him for a long time but couldn't because He always avoided me. However, perhaps He heard my prayer so He stopped as if waiting. I gathered all my courage to hug Him, but once again I found myself unable to hold His hand nor see His face.

I stood still in frustration and suddenly shouted loudly, for a long time:

- Sun God! Where are you?

My scream was lost in the middle of the vast desert and then died away, leaving only the rolling sand dunes standing blankly as if challenging.

But right at that moment, I suddenly became aware of a voiceless voice right next to my ear: "It's me!".

My soul suddenly seemed to be expanded, the disappointment automatically disappeared, and I clearly felt a strange scene appearing. A glorious, shining scene appeared before me, and suddenly I realized that I could not find Him on the outside but had to find Him on the inside. As soon as I thought like that, it was as if an invisible hand had removed the cloth that had been covering my eyes for a long time. For a long time I have been searching for the Sun through rituals in the temple. I searched for Him through ritual offerings, but He always eluded me. Now, in the middle of this vast desert, He is again present next to me and whispers clearly in my ear:

“Why have you been so busy looking for Me on the outside?

Turn inside, you will meet Me!” .

I was speechless in that strange moment of ecstasy and naturally understood that up until now I had been searching outside so I had no results, the answer only came from within and if I knew how to turn inside my inner world - all questions seemed to be answered. People often have the habit of being dependent and wanting to seek outside help, but sometimes they themselves have enough strength and intuitive reasoning to solve the problem.

I was ecstatic in this magical magic, time seemed to stand still, then my mind swirled with countless thoughts that needed to be answered. I thought of the clergy who supported me to ascend to the throne of Pharaoh, they did so only for their own benefit. Building temples and organizing offerings of offerings is just a form of profiteering by this group. This is a mistake because in reality, the Sun God does not reside in those huge temples that are being built, but He always resides in my mind and in the hearts of everyone. The long-unanswered question was suddenly answered naturally. I felt a deep peace arise within me. My breath gradually became lighter, escaping from my lungs like a cool breeze. My soul was no longer as disturbed as before but became extremely calm. I was no longer conscious of my body, my mind became unusually clear. My arrogant and violent ego naturally disappeared into the vast desert. My eyes widened, I saw where the light of the sun spread and life burst forth. I saw date palm roots growing under the sand in oases in the desert. Looking far away, I saw merchant caravans riding camels leaning on the roads leading to the capital Thebes. In my eyes, everything becomes more alive than ever. Even my body dissolved into this vast, endless stream of light. I was ecstatic in this magical feeling and suddenly understood that the Sun is the source of boundless peace, His entire body is woven with countless rays of light. The entire universe appears in this stream of light with countless shining stars everywhere. Why did He do that? The answer came to me immediately: “I am love” .

At that moment, I realized that it was love that gave Cihone the strength to help sick children. I thought of the old doctor's words about children lacking love. I understand that I am also a victim of this because I lost my mother at a young age and why I became a more violent person than the previous Pharaohs. I don't know how long I was immersed in this state, but I received the answer I had been wondering about for a long time.

* * *

I suddenly woke up and found myself sitting in my office in New York. The strange feeling of peace in the desert still leaves wonderful vibrations in my mind. I wonder if I just had a real past life experience or was it just a dream? But a dream cannot be so clear in every detail and have such deep echoes.

Usually after a dream people forget immediately, but these experiences and emotions stay with me forever after. But when I raised my hand to look at the scarab ring on my finger and tried to focus my thoughts on it, I couldn't feel anything. Why could I remember and relive my past life just by looking at it, but now I can't?

During that day, my mind was completely dominated by the events that took place in my subconscious life in Egypt. If I have the ability to remember past lives, I should know what happened after that, right? Will I get to see that gentle girl, Cihone, again? What happened to the Egyptian dynasty after that?

The next day, I continued to look at the ring hoping it could take me back to my past life but it still didn't happen as expected. After many futile attempts, I thought of Mr. Kris.

If this man can help me remember my past life in Atlantis, then maybe he can also help me return to my past life in Egypt?

During the talk about his life in Egypt, Thomas said that although in the last moments in Atlantis, he began to be aware of feelings of regret and love, but it was not clear. It was just a seed planted in his subconscious. In this life, through contact with Cihone, he learned that love is something we give unconditionally, so he began to transform. From this understanding, he became more aware of the Sun and experienced magic in the desert. From there, he clearly understood the depravity of the ancient religion that was being manipulated by the clerical factions of Thebes without paying any attention to the lives of poor people.

noi_dung:
PART FIVE

PHARAOH

POWER AND LOVE

That afternoon, I flew a plane straight to Colorado. As soon as I stopped the car in front of Mr. Kris's house, I saw him open the door and step out. After a few polite greetings, I briefly told Mr. Kris about my recent experience, then asked:

- You said before that you would help me remember my past life, so how did this happen?

Mr. Kris did not answer immediately but leisurely invited me into the house, took a plate of fresh fruit and invited me to eat. Despite my restless and impatient behavior, Mr. Kris remained calm:

- I can help because you told me before. Actually, you have to develop the ability yourself that you forgot in this life.

I wonder:

- But what should I do?

Mr. Kris leisurely replied:

- In the past, he had this ability when his mind was quiet while meditating. Now that he has let his desires dictate him, with such a disturbed mind, how can he restore this ability?

We looked at each other silently for a few minutes, Mr. Kris's words really had a reassuring effect on me. I exclaimed:

- It is truly a coincidence that we meet again in this life.

Mr. Kris smiled:

- So you must agree that we have gone through many lives before? Did you believe that there is a Law of Reincarnation?

I smiled confusedly and didn't say anything. Mr. Kris continued:

- Dear friend, this is not an accident, it was pre-arranged

. Due to the influence of the dynamics in the universe through the laws of Samsara and Karma, one person meets another. Sometimes it's debt, sometimes it's fate, sometimes we meet to repay debt, sometimes we meet to reconnect with old relationships. So many things that happen in life seem random but are actually pre-arranged by cause and effect to bring about certain results.

Listening to Mr. Kris, my heart was incredibly moved. Up to this point, I no longer have any doubts but completely believe that there is the law of Reincarnation and Cause and Effect.

Mr. Kris looked at me mischievously and then spoke:

- It seems like you are wondering about a girl and don't know how this love affair will end, right?

I was startled, wondering how he knew that. As if reading my thoughts, Mr. Kris smiled:

- I can know what you are thinking.

I deliberately deflected the words:

- Actually, I was wondering about the religion that worships the sun god Amun Ra because I just had a strange experience reminiscing about my past life in Egypt.

Mr. Kris explained:

- The Sun God Ra is just an ancient concept referring to the

creation of the universe. It originated from the ancient religion of Atlantis, then passed to Egypt by those who escaped the great flood and settled there. At first it included many fields such as astronomy, medicine, mathematics, architecture, music, etc. but over time, some scientific fields were lost. The Egyptians only knew the sun god Ra as the creator, just like today we use the word "God". Egyptian religion at that time worshiped many gods such as river gods, mountain gods, earth gods, desert gods and local gods. The priests in Thebes worshiped Amun, a local god, but when the influence of this group grew stronger and was respected by the Pharaohs, they changed the name of this god to Amun Ra, promoting him to become a supreme god for all Egyptians to worship, thus expanding the power of the clergy. Since then, this country lost the quintessence of the previous era and went down the path of devout religion, then gradually became superstitious and no longer a science as before.

Mr. Kris continued to explain:

- In ancient times, Egypt was a rich land running along the Nile River with vast fields, ponds and lakes full of fish and shrimp. The people of this country lived peacefully and were influenced by the religion of worshiping the Sun god, originating from Atlantis. The ancient Egyptian kings all came from Atlantis, so they had knowledge of the natural dynamics hidden in the universe and knew how to control the energies coming from the stars to receive cosmic lines for special rituals. Therefore, if one studies carefully, one will see that the pyramid was built in a certain position to receive cosmic energy, not a royal tomb as archaeologists often say.

I was surprised:

- But I heard that it was the burial place of the bodies of ancient Pharaohs

.

Mr. Kris shook his head:

- That was a disastrous misunderstanding. Because currently no one knows exactly what purpose the pyramid was built for, so everything is just a hypothesis. When an archaeologist speculated that it was the tomb of a Pharaoh, and then other archaeologists followed suit, public opinion agreed without requiring any further evidence.

Mr. Kris explained:

- If one observes closely, one can see a difference between the tombs of kings in the valley of kings' tombs and the pyramids.

The mausoleums always have drawings and sculptures on the cliffs to remember and praise the merits of those kings, along with charms, religious rituals, images of the dead being judged by the god Osiris in the underworld, etc. In addition, the coffins also have many overlapping layers of sarcophagi and a lot of furniture, wealth, gold, silver and jewels buried with them. Hundreds of tombs in the valley of the king's tomb are all decorated in the same way. Meanwhile, all the cliffs in the pyramid are completely empty, with absolutely no drawings or signs at all. Has anyone asked why there is such a difference?

Egyptian religion advocates that in tombs must be clearly marked symbols with spells, incantations, and the Book of the Dead [7] fin order to bring the souls of the dead to the afterlife, why are there no images in the pyramids? photos or any writing? Why did people put so much effort into building a huge, great building but inside it was empty, with nothing at all, no image, no trace, no writing? So it was built for something other than a tomb.

Currently, archaeologists believe that the great pyramid built in the Giza region is the tomb of the Pharaohs named Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure, but has anyone ever found the mummies of these kings there? Egyptian history also does not record anything about the reigns of these kings, although since ancient times Egyptians have known how to write history and record the kings' victories in temples or tombs. If these kings built such great works, they must have been special kings, but why are there no books, documents or documents about them and only a few fragmentary anecdotes? Does anyone know why this is so?

Most ancient documents about Egypt clearly record the architectural works in the valley of the king's tomb, including the names of the architects and priests in charge of that work, but no document has been found mentioning the process of building the pyramids or how it was completed? Why is there such an omission?

The Giza pyramid was built of giant stones, perfectly stacked on top of each other, without an inch of deviation.

Each rock weighs hundreds of tons, so how can people carry thousands of such great rocks stacked up so high? Even if there were hundreds of thousands of slaves pulling these rocks up, it would be impossible to do so with human strength alone.

Today, with the most modern machinery, humans cannot do that job, let alone thousands of years ago? So who built these pyramids and what techniques were used?

The stones to build the pyramids were carved from mountains hundreds of miles away. How could people transport thousands of these giant stones to the middle of the Giza desert when the Egyptians at that time did not know how to use wheels or cranes? Could it be that the ancients used some technique from another civilization that no one knows about today?

Mr. Kris stopped, looked at me, smiled and added:

- Currently, in the jungles of Africa and South America, there are countless pyramids, similar to those in Egypt, that have just been discovered.

The tribes living in that area all say it is the temple of their ancestors, a place to practice religious rituals, but no one says it is the tomb of kings. Why do archaeologists believe that the Egyptian pyramids were the tombs of kings while the South American pyramids were just places of worship? Has anyone asked why there is such a difference?

Think about it, these primitive tribes, living in huts made of leaves, knowing nothing about architecture or mathematics, how could their ancestors build pyramids with such giant rocks? Unless this knowledge comes from a once flourishing civilization or a certain race of people that has now disappeared from the face of the earth.

As you know, to avoid the great flood, the Atlanteans built boats to settle around the world and brought their religion with them. If you pay attention, you will see that all places with pyramids worship the Sun god, or the sun symbol. Why in places thousands of miles away do people there not worship any other gods but all worship the Sun God if it does not come from a common origin?

Listening to Mr. Kris's detailed presentation like that, I realized that there are clear differences in the hypotheses of archaeologists that today most people believe without verifying whether those hypotheses are true or false. Perhaps only when people can go back in time, back to the past, can they clearly understand the meaning of the existence of these pyramids.

I wonder:

- I remembered my previous life in Atlantis, but now I experience another life in Egypt. The time in Atlantis happened about twelve thousand years BC, then in Egypt about three thousand years BC, so what happened between those two lives? Will I still live somewhere else?

Mr. Kris looked at me intently, then seriously asked:

- Do you really want to know that? Does he have the courage to accept the truth?

I'm surprised:

- Why not? If a person dies and is reborn in another life, how long is the time between the two lives?

Mr. Kris looked at me hesitantly, then explained:

- Hey friend, before we talked about the law of Reincarnation. People are born and die, die and are reborn again, wandering around in the cycle of Samsara - but not everyone is reborn as a human. Depending on complex reasons, people can sometimes be reborn as animals, demons, or other creatures. You should know that the realm we live in is not the only realm, there are realms of other living beings that we cannot see. We can call them different dimensions or invisible worlds because our current senses cannot perceive all of these worlds. However, being invisible does not mean they are not present with us.

Previously I talked about the change or evolution from metal to herbs, then to lower organisms (like insects). These species have a common store of experience so they act exactly the same. This storehouse accumulates learning experiences for insects, and then they transform into animals like birds, then reptiles, then beasts, etc. Then, this experience is personalized into intelligent creatures such as cattle or buffaloes, dogs and cats, etc. This personalized understanding helps creatures continue to evolve and transform into humans with intelligent minds that can think and discriminate. The change from low-level animals to humans is called by today's science the law of Evolution.

Mr. Kris looked at me as if to make sure I understood what he said, then continued:

- However, if there is evolution, there must also be degeneration, meaning change from intelligent species to low-level species. One big intelligence can turn into many small intelligences. Therefore, when a person degenerates into an animal, knowledge also follows those incarnations, not becoming a single animal but often becoming many animals. If not, then wouldn't an animal be as intelligent as a human?

Let's take the example of a person reincarnating into ten dogs, each of which only has one-tenth of that person's intelligence because the intelligence has been divided into ten parts. During this separation process, understanding must be impaired, so these dogs cannot be as intelligent as humans.

Over millions of years, developing from low-level species to humans, creatures must go through so many lives, learn so many things, and purify so many things to transform into humans. People with intelligent minds, knowing how to distinguish between good and right, must continue to learn to advance to higher positions, to become saints. The unfortunate thing is that instead of learning to understand more, they act ignorantly, so they have to reincarnate again to learn more lessons that they lack.

Mr. Kris paused as if to let me think, then continued:

- Samsara can be temporarily considered as a big school, in which all living beings must learn until they reach complete understanding.

Evolution or degeneration is an important factor to ensure that the organism has learned the lesson. If you have not learned it thoroughly, you must learn it again, and that is the principle of the law of Cause and Effect. Whatever you sow, you will reap. Any action that occurs has a response, sometimes it happens immediately, sometimes it happens later, in another life.

Smart people will quickly learn from their mistakes, then change themselves to avoid making them again. Those who do not know how to learn from their mistakes will have to learn over and over again, through many lives, until they learn the lesson they are supposed to learn. Ignorant people will live by instinct instead of using their intelligent brains, and they often reincarnate back into animals. Because their minds are not fully developed and have not learned clear lessons, they must continue to learn for many lives as different animals before returning to being human.

However, when a person reincarnates into many animals, their intelligence is divided into ten, hundreds, thousands, or millions of parts, their understanding also decreases, so they have to go through many lifetimes to learn before they can reincarnate back into humans. The more the understanding from past learning experiences is reduced, the more ignorant the creature becomes, living hundreds of thousands of miserable lives, today being this animal, tomorrow being another animal, just floating in the animal life, it is not easy to return to be reincarnated into a human body. Because understanding has been separated into hundreds, thousands of pieces, it is not easy to put it back together again?

For example, greedy people often turn into maggots, eating dirty places. Their knowledge has been divided among millions of maggots. What else do these stupid insects know? Therefore, they will have to go through many lives, going from one animal species to another to develop their understanding, then they can evolve into humans.

For insects and insects, their lives only last a few days, so they will have to go through hundreds of thousands of insect lives, for a long time before they can regain the understanding to transform into humans. You should know that becoming human is not easy at all and once you lose your human body, it is very difficult to return. This is a very important thing that not many people know.

I asked again:

- So what about my case? After my life in Atlantis, where did I go and what did I do?

Mr. Kris explained:

- The reason I haven't answered your question right away is because I have to briefly explain

the Law of Reincarnation, with the two main elements being evolution and degeneration, so that you can clearly understand what I am about to say next.

Mr. Kris looked at me with pity, then continued:

- During my human life in Atlantis, where scientific understanding was very high, few people knew how to learn or develop love. Due to this shortcoming, he, like everyone else at that time, lived indifferently, selfishly, greedily, and was influenced by the surrounding environment. He was born into a high-class family, with the right to exploit and appropriate things from lower-class people, which was the law of the strong in Atlantis society at that time. Therefore, he was not aware of his actions. He caused suffering and disadvantage to others, so he created bad karma, so he had to suffer the consequences.

In his case, when he saw Kor's bare feet, he was infatuated and wanted to possess her. That greedy thought leads to a crazy thought, starting the evil actions that follow. Even though he was trained to become a physician, he practiced the pagan methods of Og - such as killing animals to sacrifice to the gods, using spells to bewitch people's minds, using drugs to achieve sexual desires. Because of this blind understanding, his mind became crazy and created huge negative karma. Do you want me to say more?

I looked at Mr. Kris, his eyes lit up strangely, his whole body exuded a serious aura. I breathed heavily:

- Yes, please just say it. I'm ready to listen.

Mr. Kris continued in a majestic voice:

- He used evil magic to usurp the pure nun in the Sun temple, so he had to suffer the consequences and reincarnated as a insect that sucks blood and pus from women's feet. The reason was because he was so infatuated with Kor's bare feet that his thoughts kept pursuing and clinging to women's feet. After dying in the great flood, he transformed into millions of insects, living in the mangy feet of women. He had to spend millions of lives as an insect just because of that blind delusion.

Surely you already know that people have thoughts of desiring whatever they like. Because of their passion for women's feet, it haunted him for thousands of years as a worm.

Mr. Kris's words were a thunderous sound, making me stunned, unable to say anything for a long time. Mr. Kris was silent, looking intently at me, his eyes becoming softer.

When I regained my composure, Mr. Kris leisurely said:

- He has gone through many lives on the path of evolution from

insects to animals before being returned to the human body. However, the life in Atlantis was not your first life, there were many previous lives that you cannot remember now. During those lives, he helped many people and sowed a lot of good karma.

Thanks to these special conditions, when he reincarnated as a human, he became a Pharaoh ruling a large kingdom, enjoying all joys. However, in his heart there were still cruel traits originating from his life in Atlantis, so he became a dictatorial ruler. Before dying in Atlantis, he felt remorse and love for Kor. This is a very powerful transformational power, because the Atlanteans at that time did not know regret or love.

It was because of this rare fate that after experiencing many animal lives, he was reborn as a human in Egypt to continue the lesson he needed to learn.

I hesitantly asked:

- So what did I learn when I was reincarnated in Egypt?

Mr. Kris looked at me attentively:

- He was born in the twenty-third dynasty during the final period of ancient kings in Egypt. At that time, Egypt was degraded and exhausted, as a result of the construction of mausoleums and tombs for previous Pharaohs. At this time, most of the Pharaohs could not sit on the throne for long because of disputes between the clergy and the Pharaohs. In the final stage, the culture of this country declined; The people are poor and miserable; corrupt officials; Evil tyrants emerged and appropriated people's property, land, houses, fields, and gardens; Witchcraft is popular; The clergy hold the power of life and death; The Pharaohs were incompetent, no one could rule for long.

I wonder:

- But what about my case? How can I remember my past life in Egypt?

Mr. Kris smiled:

- Tonight, when your mind is at ease, I will help you return to the memories of that life. Now you should rest and relax because you were tired from flying the plane here.

That evening, after eating some fruit, Mr. Kris asked me to sit still in the armchair and meditate for a while, then walked over and whispered a sentence in my ear in a strange language that made me fall asleep and return to my memories of the past in Egypt.

* * *

I found myself returning to the palace after having a strange experience

search in the desert. As soon as I arrived, I immediately met a number of leaders waiting there. Amed, the commander, reported:

- Dear Pharaoh, as usual every year, we send troops to conquer the surrounding countries. Currently, there is a shortage of funds, not enough for forging weapons and war vehicles. We asked Pharaoh to raise taxes to have enough money for this.

According to the precedent of previous Pharaohs, every year Egypt sent troops to conquer surrounding countries and brought back many spoils such as gold, silver, resources and slaves. Even though I had only been on the throne for a few months, I had prepared for this conquest, but now there was a shortage of funds due to too much temple construction.

I called Satt in. As soon as he arrived, I immediately asked:

- Have you investigated those who abused public construction funds?

Satt replied:

- Dear Pharaoh! I have found one construction abuser but need time to investigate the others.

I couldn't wait to shake my head:

- If we prolong the time, where will we get the funds to forge weapons for the upcoming war? Without weapons, it is impossible to win and bring back gold, silver, and slaves for you to build the temple.

We cannot let this construction affect the military's fighting ability.

Satt looked at me coldly, then said:

- This one has investigated the construction of a tomb for Pharaoh. The following is a report about Setau, the architect who oversaw the construction of his mausoleum. I have clear evidence that Setau took away some of the materials to build his own grave.

I held the report, looked at the numbers of materials and slaves that had been mutilated by Setau and the testimonies of witnesses involved. Satt observed me carefully, then said:

- Please Pharaoh judge this criminal.

I thought to myself: "This priest really has the skills. While I wanted to investigate the construction of the temple by the clergy, he instead investigated the construction of my mausoleum and found a criminal - what a cunning diversion."

Of course, embezzling funds to build a Pharaoh's tomb is a serious crime, unforgivable. With such clear evidence, I cannot do anything other than sentence Setau to death immediately. Immediately, I shouted:

- Where are the soldiers! Immediately capture Setau and throw him into the lion's den! His family members must be banished to the desert and never return.

However, not willing to lose this game, I continued to shout:

- Hey Satt! Your investigation is just the first step, there are probably others out there. From now on, I want to personally investigate the temple construction project of the priests to punish those who are greedy and abuse their power to violate the law!

The entire court was immediately shocked because everyone knew that once I personally investigated, there were definitely many people thrown into the lion's den. They saw clearly how angry I was when I enacted strict laws. I raised the king's seal of authority:

- This is my order! Immediately stop the temple construction work until we have finished investigating everything.

Amed stepped out:

- Dear Pharaoh! The investigation will take time. Please increase taxes immediately so we can prepare to forge weapons.

I was about to agree right away, but for some reason, at that moment, I thought of the story I had with the old doctor the other day about increasing taxes and making people more miserable. I shook my head:

- That's for later. Currently, we prioritize investigating the construction first.

Amed quickly whispered:

- We need weapons to prepare for the war before the rainy season comes. If it is slow, the chariots cannot move on the mud.

As a military commander, of course I knew this, but because I had decided to strike, I shouted:

- This is my order! You can't say anything anymore!

After giving the order, I walked into the palace even though the military officials were bewildered because no one expected my reaction to be so drastic.

Satt followed:

- Dear Pharaoh, why did you stop the construction?

I turned around and looked him straight in the face, saying each word:

- I have my reasons! Do you want to betray me?

Satt stepped back, his face pale:

- No! Never. We helped you ascend to the throne of Pharaoh, so why would we betray you?

I chuckled:

- If you had ever plotted treason, why would you still have your head on your neck now?

Satt gasped:

- Dear Pharaoh, that's right. But why did he stop the construction of the temple?

I got angry:

- As Pharaoh, whatever I want is my right! I can also destroy all your temples and kill not a single cleric left.

Satt retreated and leaned his back against the wall, his face turning gray because he knew my stubborn and violent nature:

- Pharaoh should calm down. We have agreed that when Pharaoh takes the throne, he will build many temples everywhere. Have you forgotten? If all construction stops, it will leave thousands of workers without work. Then what will they use to live? There will definitely be chaos. I'm afraid this will do more harm than good.

Satt's words startled me and I thought for a moment, but the order was issued and could not be taken back. I continued:

- I know that well, but I want to consider why we built so many temples.

Satt lowered his voice and begged:

- Please consider carefully, Pharaoh, stopping the construction of the temple will cause a lot of chaos. For many years, construction has been an important job that has nurtured countless workers and slaves. We can't leave them without a job.

I glared:

- I've decided. Do you still dare to disobey my orders?

Satt tried to explain:

- That's not true. But we also need to continue building his mausoleum. If Setau is executed, someone else must be found to replace him. He needed to prepare for life in the afterlife. What do you think when you meet the gods that you just forced to stop building their temples?

His words made me even angrier, I shouted:

- Do you think I don't know that you have built hundreds of temples and nurtured thousands of clergy and their relatives? Why has the number of temples and priests increased so much in just a short period of time? Did the priests have more wives and slaves than the Pharaoh? Who rules Egypt? Pharaoh or priest?

My words hit Satt right in the heart, he was really scared and didn't dare to say anything else. I silently walked into the harem and left him standing there.

For all Egyptian Pharaohs, the most important thing when ascending the throne is to build a great tomb for themselves to ensure life in the afterlife. Therefore, finding an architect to build the mausoleum early on is a priority, because the project often lasts for many years. The larger the mausoleum, the longer it takes to build, sometimes lasting several decades. No one knows how long Pharaoh can live, but if he dies and the tomb is not yet completed, it will be unfortunate. Because without a beautiful grave, there cannot be a good life in the afterlife. However, finding a replacement architect is not easy because this project is always kept secret. Only the Pharaoh and the architect or a few people involved in the construction know clearly. The tombs of the Egyptian Pharaohs are all dug deep into the cliffs in a place called the king's tomb valley, with soldiers carefully guarding them. Every tomb is designed with many special details to prevent theft. In the tomb there are many different rooms and passages with traps to deceive grave robbers and only the architect knows these traps. Therefore, replacing the architect when the construction is still unfinished is an extremely complicated and difficult problem.

However, the next morning, Satt brought in a new, tall architect. Satt said:

- Dear Pharaoh, Samut here worked as Setau's assistant in construction projects at Kanak and Luxor before, so he is familiar with the construction projects left by Setau. Please Pharaoh employ this person.

As soon as I saw Samut, I was startled because it was the young man I met at the old doctor's house with Cihone the day before. Of course, Samut didn't recognize me at that time, partly because it was dark that day, I covered part of my face and was wearing an old cloak.

And now I was sitting on the majestic throne, so Samut didn't dare look at me for long but knelt down and waited for orders.

I hesitated:

- Do you know how complicated this construction is?

Satt hastily replied:

- I showed Samut the construction project and he knew every detail. Because he had worked with Setau before, he also knew the abilities of the people working under him. It's hard to find someone better these days. Please Pharaoh allow him to take over this job.

While I was thinking, Samut said:

- Dear Pharaoh, I have looked at Setau's construction project and know clearly how this job must be done.

Satt continued:

- Each architect has different designs and ideas, finding new people to continue this unfinished work can delay construction. Please Pharaoh decide.

Faced with such an important matter, of course I could not delay the construction of my tomb, so I had to approve Samut to do it. Workers building the Pharaoh's tomb had to work in the valley of the king's tomb, quite far from the capital Thebes, so these people brought their families to stay in a small nearby village called Deir el-Medina. Not long after, I called Erhu, a trusted detective:

- I want you to monitor the workers building my tomb, and let me know if anything unusual happens. I want to know the details so no one can cheat again.

Erhu laughed:

- After Setau's death, I guarantee that no one will dare to play tricks again, Pharaoh.

I added:

- I want to know about Samut, see how he works.

Erhu reports:

- After being entrusted with higher responsibilities with a generous salary as an architect. Samut got married right away and moved to live in Deir el-Medina near the construction site.

I asked:

- Who is in his family?

The detective replied:

- There was only him and a young wife there.

I didn't say anything more, but a strange feeling suddenly arose in my heart because I knew that the girl I was very sympathetic to belonged to someone else.

A few days later, Satt walked in to present a report:

Instead of getting angry, I coldly said:

Although annoyed, Satt also arranged a group of soldiers to escort me and Queen Nedjem to the valley of the king's tomb.

Being informed that Pharaoh was coming, Samut rushed to welcome him. - That is Samut's wife. At mealtimes, the masons' wives had to bring food, but only the old people.

Very few young wives dare to venture into the crowd of young workers without fear of being teased or harassed. However, this girl is different, not because she is Samut's wife, in the past Setau's wife did not dare to come here but...

I asked urgently:

- But what to do?

- This girl is different, does Pharaoh see it? She brought a lot of food to give to unmarried people who had no one to take care of food and to the elderly whose old wife could not travel from Deir el-Medina village to come here. No one had ever done that before.

I watched Cihone take care of the injured people, she bandaged them and kindly talked to them and encouraged them. The workers standing around looked at her with appreciation because she spoke gently and gently to each person. No one has a rude attitude towards that lovely girl.

I was watching Cihone when suddenly there was a noise, then the sound of a woman screaming nearby. I saw the soldiers trying to pull that woman away. Erhu ran to see and reported:

- Dear Pharaoh, that is Setau's wife. According to your order, Setau's entire family must be banished to the desert, but she escaped.

- How did she hide here these past few days without anyone knowing? She must be forced

exiled to the desert.

I looked at Cihone thoughtfully comforting this woman and suddenly thought of the concept of love that I had talked about with the old physician the day before. I was still thinking when Cihone suddenly came forward and knelt down in front of me:

Cihone's words surprised me and had a strange power. I nodded and raised my hand to instruct:

- Okay, I allow you to stay in Deir el-Medina to give birth, and then serve your sentence later.

Setau's wife happily knelt down, mumbled a few words of thanks and then left. Cihone also followed. I wistfully watched her figure disappear behind the desert sand dunes.

For several weeks now, the suspension of temple construction projects has created a stream of unfavorable public opinion in the kingdom because workers and slaves suddenly have no work to earn a living. I have had sleepless nights because I kept thinking about these things. What will their future be like when living conditions become difficult, and what will happen to children who do not grow up carefully?

I felt sad thinking about my powerful position as Pharaoh and the loneliness in this palace full of beautiful women and then suddenly wondered if Cihone remembered or thought anything of me? I thought of the Sun God and my strange experience in the desert, as well as the waste of resources on huge temples for the priests who had brought me to the position I am today. I thought about the concept of love in life that I had never known before and the beautiful girl who used love to take care of sick children. I thought to myself, if I could be a commoner like Samut and have a wife like Cihone, how happy I would be.

I shouted angrily:

I got angry:

- I know our marriage is just an arrangement for

you to ascend to the throne of Pharaoh, but I accept it. I laughed out loud:

Nedjem is still patient and gentle:

- Please Pharaoh, don't misunderstand what I mean. I know you didn't pay attention to me before and now you have noticed another girl.

Nedjem looked at me and smiled discreetly:

Nedjem is still gentle:

Nedjem's unexpected way of speaking, full of sincerity and concern, made me flustered. Nedjem continued:

I'm really confused:

Queen Nedjem's every word startled me. Nedjem remained calm:

Cihone timidly:

Nedjem said loudly:

Nedjem calmly:

All that night I kept thinking about the clergy, about Cihone and Nedjem's conversation until nearly morning before I fell asleep.

According to custom in Thebes, the statue of the god Amun Ra was carefully kept in a closed room, only a few high-ranking clergy were allowed to enter it. Once a year, this statue was taken out and held in procession around Thebes to bless the people. This is an important ceremony, at which people bring offerings to make offerings when this statue is carried through the neighborhood where they live. This is also the time when people direct their prayers to this god. The procession was held with great solemnity and solemnity. The statue was placed on a large palanquin carried by ten priests. Behind the palanquin is a set of gong and drum musicians led by an elderly priest. Finally, there is the palanquin of the Pharaoh and the queen, along with the court officials. People in the street display large carpets in front of their houses with offerings. When the procession passes, a group of clergy following will collect the offerings and bring them to the temple for distribution. cause more disturbances and disadvantages. We can't do that.

those who abuse public funds. I want you to bring the list of those illegals to me for trial, otherwise I will immediately take strong measures against you.

As soon as I arrived, I was told by the servant that Queen Nedjem had invited me to her private room because there were guests coming to visit. Of course I immediately guessed who it was. Like last time, I stood behind the curtain and watched Nedjem converse with Cihone. Cihone spoke to Nedjem more confidently this time.

- I know you also have the ability to heal children.

I didn't expect you to have so many talents. Where did you learn these things?

- I wasn't taught anything by anyone. I only know how to love children.

Cihone shook her head:

- No one told me to do that. I only know how to love, and feel that once loved, people can be stronger and healthier, and so can children.

and wants her to completely belong to her, then as you said, that woman's love in return will make the man stronger. What will you think?

- Dear Queen, I don't know if it is true love, or if it is a possession - possession will cause suffering. Love must be from both sides and cannot cause pain to others.

Cihone's words shocked me because I have never heard anyone speak so clearly before. The secret desire to have Cihone naturally melted away like water bubbles. Nedjem was also silent and surprised by the answer, but continued to ask:

- If a woman sacrificed herself for another man even though that man did not pay attention to her, would you consider that love?

I suddenly realized that Nedjem was talking about her situation.

Cihone spoke:

- Dear Queen, true love cannot create suffering but only brings joy. If sacrifice causes suffering and pain, it is something other than true love.

Nedjem was silent and then sighed:

- You're such a strange person, I've never heard anyone talk like that

. If so, what is love?

Cihone replied:

- I only know how to love unconditionally.

Cihone's words make me think of the voiceless voice of the Sun - “I am love.” - and suddenly understood that He did not ask for anything because He is love. I thought of the demands of the clergy, the offerings, the magnificent temples, the gardens of the clergy's family and the workers and slaves brought to serve these people.

I stood there but my mind was transformed with chaotic thoughts.

Busy in thought, I heard Nedjem ask:

- If so, what is the love between husband and wife? Can people love each other like that?

Cihone accidentally said:

- If they love sincerely, without clinging or asking for anything, then that is true love. If they cling to or depend on something, it is just attraction, because if they are not close to each other and are not rewarded, they will suffer. True love cannot lead to suffering. People who know how to love each other like that, even if they are apart, their love for each other will never change.

Nedjem exclaimed:

- What you say is very interesting, but who taught you that?

How do you know these things?

Cihone replied:

- When I was young, I heard my adoptive parents talk about this, but then I felt it was my natural nature. My adoptive father was trained at the Thai Duong temple, preparing to become a priest, but due to disagreements with the temple's teachings, he became a physician.

- What did your parents teach you?

I stood still, but my mind was completely shocked. Suddenly my whole body trembled as if a strong electric current ran through me because all the questions and things I wanted to know had been fully answered. Wherever the anger suddenly welled up, the ferocious and insolent blood of the Kusk race flowed through my veins, making me grit my teeth: "Impossible! The streams of decisive thoughts ran as fast as lightning in my head, forgetting the presence of Cihone and Queen Nedjem, clutching the precious sword, I let out a scream that echoed throughout the palace...

Suddenly I felt a very strong force hitting my chest, making me dizzy, my head spinning, my eyes closed... and then, I woke up and suddenly found myself drenched in sweat sitting back, holding my hands tightly. into the armchair at Mr. Kris's house.

I sat up in shock, rubbed my eyes, saw Mr. Kris sitting across from me, and shouted loudly:

- Why is this Mr. Kris? I'm in the palace, so why am I here now? How long has it been since I left this room?

- He was fortunate enough to go on a journey to explore his own past many hundreds of years ago in Egypt. He must have realized what he wanted to learn during his life there. - But I want to know what happened to me after that? What is the next situation in Egypt? Everything is unfinished there.

What did I do to the clergy? Queen Nedjem, the girl Cihone... what happened to them after that?

Mr. Kris squinted at me and said leisurely:

- Now it's good that you still remember Cihone. What a rare power of love for a lonely Pharaoh. Before answering your questions, I want to talk about Egypt so you can relate and understand better. In ancient times, Egypt consisted of many tribes living on the banks of the Nile River. The land was fertile due to alluvial deposits, making agricultural cultivation convenient and life easy and peaceful.
